name: NFPA 70, National Electrical Code (USA)
references: NFPA 70, National Electrical Code, 2014 edition, 220.84 and Table 220.84 (the optional calculation for three or more multifamily dwelling units)
note: A building's demand by this country's method (`building_demand`). The rest of the discipline comes from BIMCraft's library, and says so.

building_demand.source: NFPA 70, National Electrical Code, 2014 edition, 220.84 and Table 220.84 (the optional calculation for three or more multifamily dwelling units): the connected load of all the units, each worked out as 220.84(C) says, times a demand factor by their number; the house loads apart, by Part III. The 2026 edition moves Article 220's load calculations to Article 120 (120.84).

dwelling.source: NEC 220.84(C): each unit's connected load (general lighting and receptacles by floor area, small-appliance and laundry circuits, appliances, cooking, heating or air conditioning), worked out by the designer and given here as its `demand`

diversity.source: NEC Table 220.84 (2014): the demand factor by the number of dwelling units, 45 % for 3 to 5 down to 23 % for 62 and over

notes: Only where no unit is fed by more than one feeder, each unit has electric cooking and each has electric space heating, air conditioning or both (220.84(A)).
The house loads (corridor lighting, lifts, pumps) go in `common_demand`, worked out by Part III with its own demand factors (220.84(B)).

The 2026 edition changed what a unit's load counts (general lighting 2 VA/ft², a charger at its nameplate), not this table's bands as far as checked; give the unit's `demand` by the edition the jurisdiction adopted.
not_covered: each unit's load itself (220.84(C), or 120.84 in the 2026 edition), which comes in as its `demand`
two dwelling units (220.85) and the exception for units without electric cooking (220.84(A)(2))
the neutral (220.61) and the service conductors and equipment the load asks

Cu THHN 90 °C.note: NFPA 70 (NEC) Table 310.16, 90 °C column, 30 °C ambient, up to three current-carrying conductors in a raceway. Sizes are AWG or kcmil, kept in mm².

Cu THW 75 °C.note: NFPA 70 (NEC) Table 310.16, 75 °C column, 30 °C ambient, up to three current-carrying conductors in a raceway. Sizes are AWG or kcmil, kept in mm².
